predecessors.note: Rebuilt and resettled on the orders of Harun al-Rashid in 787/8 'by Faraj ibn Sulaym al-Khadim'; a first attempt in 778/9 'was apparently not completed'. Cilicia had been a depopulated march between the empires; Cliopatria's Abbasid Caliphate row starts in 750 (eu-me-08).

land.text: 'The Byzantine emperor Nikephoros II Phokas captured the city and the rest of Cilicia, ending Muslim rule there' (16 August 965)

capitals.name: Tarsus
capitals.note: The Emirate_of_Tarsus page (which serves the content of 'List of Abbasid governors of Tarsus') has no infobox and names no capital; Tarsus was the governors' seat and, on the Thughur page, the province's 'most important town'. (Reviewer eu-05-x, 2026-10-19: note rewritten: the earlier text quoted an infobox the page does not have.)

correction.text: the Cilician (Syrian) Thughur, 'Tarsus and the rest of Cilicia'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; its Abbasid Caliphate shape for 788-965 reaches the Taurus). The Cilician (Syrian) Thughur: 'Tarsus was its most important town' (Thughur page); the Tarsus page names no other town of the province and gives no area. Cilicia is the 965 conquest's 'rest of Cilicia'; the extent before 965 is an upper bound.

ledger.note: 787/8: Harun al-Rashid refounds Tarsus. 'It was not until 787/8 that the city was rebuilt and resettled by Faraj ibn Sulaym al-Khadim, on the orders of Caliph Harun al-Rashid.' The Thughur page: Tarsus garrisoned in 787/8 and the separate jund al-'Awasim created in 786 (capitals Manbij, later Antioch). Mopsuestia had been garrisoned in 703.

region.text: Cilicia, the Cilician Thughur around Tarsus

ledger.note: 787/8: the Cilician frontier zone is drawn. Bridging: the pages name no town of the province but Tarsus (Thughur page: 'Tarsus was its most important town'); the rest of Cilicia is the researcher's reading of 'the rest of Cilicia' in 965.

964: Nikephoros II Phokas invades Cilicia. The Thughur page: 'Nikephoros II Phokas captured Cilicia in 964-965, with Antioch following soon after'; Mopsuestia, Anazarbus and Tarsus are not named individually and there are no separate dates.

region.text: Tarsus and the rest of Cilicia

ledger.note: 16 August 965: Tarsus falls. 'The Byzantine emperor Nikephoros II Phokas captured the city and the rest of Cilicia, ending Muslim rule there'; the governor table ends 'early 962 - 16 Aug. 965'.
August 965: the conquest of Cilicia ends with Tarsus.
16 August 965: the Emirate of Tarsus ends. After the 964-965 losses 'the Hamdanids of Aleppo became a tributary state' (Thughur page).

wars.name: Byzantine conquest of Cilicia

zones.text: the Cilician (Syrian) Thughur, 'Tarsus and the rest of Cilicia'

wars.outcome: Nikephoros II Phokas captured Cilicia in 964-965, Tarsus on 16 August 965, and Antioch soon after; the Hamdanids of Aleppo, who had been Tarsus's overlord since 946/7, became tributary to Byzantium.
wars.note: Sayf al-Dawla (r. 946-967) had temporarily stopped the Byzantine advance.

certainty.note: A frontier march, with the Amanus separating it from the Jazira Thughur; no page gives its limits.

notes: Written by eu-05-x (additions). Cliopatria has no row. The page is the Abbasid-period history of Tarsus, and gives no area or provincial extent: Adana, Mopsuestia and Anazarbus are not mentioned. Changes of overlord are not territorial and belong in the suzerains' dossiers (vassal events with counterpart emirate-of-tarsus): the Tulunids from 878/9 (Ahmad ibn Tulun), Abbasid allegiance 882, Tulunid overlordship again in 890, Hamdanid overlordship (Sayf al-Dawla) from 946/7. After 842 the Thughur emirates (Tarsus, Malatya, Qaliqala) were semi-independent. The Jazira Thughur and the Emirate of Melitene (fell 934 to John Kourkouas) still need a dossier; the Melitene page opened is the city's article and is silent on the emirate's extent. Group: me-08 or eu-05.
